clue.text: Invective of half-a-dozen with disastrous reputation

parts.note: six is VI in Roman numerals

indicators.note: a disastrous outcome leaves things wrecked, so the letters of the next word are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone abusive, ruined in six different ways by their bad name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disastrous' rearranges REPUTATION into TUPERATION, which follows VI.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name abusive, railing language aimed at someone.

clue.text: Five is old, it must be faced!

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
taken as written
aged means old

explanation.surface: An exclamation that an elderly five must be confronted.
explanation.definitionFit: A visage is a face, so visaged describes someone having a face of a stated kind.

clue.text: Lifting the feet

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Raising one's feet off the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifting' looks physical; here it is slang for stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting is informal for stealing, and stealing is the crime of robbery.

clue.text: Small dish for Spanish campanologist

parts.note: por is the Spanish word for 'for'
a campanologist is a bell-ringer

explanation.surface: A little bowl intended for a bell-ringer from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A porringer is a shallow bowl with a handle, traditionally used for porridge or soup.

clue.text: Interjection coming from Rex first because of the smell

indicators.note: first says the king's letter comes at the front of the word

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king
eek is an interjection of alarm

explanation.surface: Rex shrieks before anyone else because of a bad odour.
explanation.definitionFit: Reek is a strong unpleasant odour, a stench.

clue.text: Mainly having no ups and downs

definitions.text: Mainly having no ups and downs

parts.words: Mainly having no ups and downs
parts.note: reads as 'mostly level', but 'Mainly' means 'of the main', the sea, whose rising and falling water is meant

explanation.definitionFit: A sea with no rising and falling of the water level lacks the regular ebb and flow caused by the moon.

clue.text: Selected work on youth in the 1950s

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a Ted or Teddy boy was a stylish British youth of the 1950s

explanation.surface: Chose to labour on a young man from the rock-and-roll era.
explanation.definitionFit: Opted means chose or picked.

clue.text: Struck when post had been cut

parts.note: a pole is a post
axed means cut

explanation.surface: Someone was hit when the mail had been reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' suggests the mail, but it is an upright stake.
explanation.definitionFit: To poleaxe is to fell with a heavy blow, as with a battleaxe.

clue.text: Stanley's reportedly taken a few lines

indicators.note: reportedly means what is heard spoken, so a word said aloud is meant

parts.note: Stan is short for Stanley, so this gives Stan's
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Stanley is said to have stolen some lines of text.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, Stan's plus A sounds like the answer; 'taken' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a verse, a group of lines in a poem.

clue.text: Lead attack using only part of weapon

definitions.meaning: to head an offensive, as a verb
the pointed metal tip of a spear

explanation.surface: Leading an assault while using only a fragment of one's arms.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead a charge is to be at its front point, and the pointed metal tip of a spear is its business end.

clue.text: Everybody in France eats river fish

indicators.note: eats means the French word takes the river letter inside it

parts.note: tout is French for all or everybody

explanation.surface: All of France dines on freshwater fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A trout is a freshwater game fish related to salmon.

clue.text: Obtained this Latin architectural style

parts.note: got means obtained
hic is Latin for this

explanation.surface: A classically educated person acquired a taste in buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: Gothic is the medieval European building style of pointed arches and ribbed vaults.

clue.text: Leg bound to be injured by club

indicators.note: something injured is damaged out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tied-up leg is sure to be hurt by a cudgel.
explanation.definitionFit: A bludgeon is a short heavy stick used as a weapon, a cudgel.

clue.text: Measure the same again, mentor concluded

indicators.note: concluded says the mentor's word comes at the end

parts.note: do, short for ditto, means the same again
a sage is a wise adviser

explanation.surface: The teacher finished by saying, take the same measurement again.
explanation.definitionFit: A dosage is the measured amount of medicine to be taken.

clue.text: An outstanding artist?

parts.note: reads as a brilliant painter, but 'outstanding' points to someone whose work literally stands out in three dimensions

explanation.definitionFit: A carver or modeller makes figures that project from or stand free of a surface.

clue.text: Lack of oxygen in the blood — it's breathtaking

definitions.text: Lack of oxygen in the blood
definitions.meaning: the medical condition of oxygen starvation
literally takes one's breath away, by suffocation

explanation.surface: A medical condition that is also, in its way, stunning.
explanation.definitionFit: This condition is suffocation, which literally stops one breathing, the literal sense of a phrase usually meaning amazing.

clue.text: He had included a table found in the bedroom

indicators.note: included means the contraction takes the single letter inside it

parts.note: he'd is the contraction of he had
taken as written
a board is a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A man had a table which was discovered in his sleeping quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the upright panel at the top end of a bed.

clue.text: Jack gets ointment in Clapham, perhaps

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
unction is an ointment or anointing oil

explanation.surface: A man named Jack buys some ointment in a south London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Clapham Junction in south London is one of Britain's busiest railway stations, where many lines meet.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapham is an example of a place where railway lines meet.

clue.text: It's old-fashioned, at university, to settle a debt

parts.note: square means stuffy or old-fashioned
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Being conventional while a student, one pays what one owes.
explanation.definitionFit: To square up is a phrasal verb meaning to pay off what is owed.

clue.text: Mark left on establishment seldom seen

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
CE is the Church of England, the Established Church

explanation.surface: A blemish remains on a building that is rarely noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'establishment' suggests a business; it is the Established Church; 'left on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarce means rare, hard to come across.

clue.text: Some slow and erratic ramble

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A leisurely walk that is unhurried and irregular.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander is to stroll aimlessly, to roam.

clue.text: Princely rule for a period?

definitions.meaning: government by a prince standing in for a monarch
a historical era, as in British history around 1811 to 1820

explanation.surface: Asking whether a prince's government was temporary.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the Prince of Wales governed for his incapacitated father George III, and that era also names a style of architecture and furniture.

clue.text: Golf stroke taken on road leading to motorway!

definitions.meaning: the shot played onto the green
a slip road giving access to a major route

explanation.surface: A golfer's shot played on a slip road to the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf this is the shot aimed at the green, and it also names a feeder road giving access to a highway.

clue.text: Ready to run?

parts.note: reads as an athlete set to race, but means beer ready to flow from a barrel

explanation.definitionFit: Beer drawn from a cask is available immediately, hence the idiom for anything readily available.

clue.text: Big Ben revived on the way out

indicators.note: revived means brought back in fresh shape, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: The famous London clock bell restored as it was declining.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Ben is the great bell in the clock tower of London's Houses of Parliament; 'revived' rearranges its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tide going out is receding, and anything declining is likewise fading away.

clue.text: I struggled clad in evergreen

parts.note: taken as written
vied means competed or struggled

explanation.surface: Someone fought while wearing green leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The evergreen here is the climbing plant that covers old walls, so the word means overgrown with it.

clue.text: Lady had drink first of all

parts.note: gin is a drink

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A woman had a drink before anyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, so the clue's lady is an example of someone so called.

clue.text: In favour of going back into Connecticut farm

indicators.note: into means the reversed word goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: CT is the abbreviation for the US state Connecticut

indicators.note: going back means the word for in favour of is read backwards

parts.note: for means in favour of

explanation.surface: Someone supports a return to a farm in New England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns FOR into ROF, which goes 'into' CT. A croft is a small Scottish smallholding.
explanation.definitionFit: A croft is a small rented holding of land, especially in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Copy left out of condition

indicators.note: out of means the letter for left is removed from the longer word

parts.note: a limitation is a condition or restriction

explanation.surface: A duplicate omitted from the terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'condition' is LIMITATION, from which L goes 'out of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A copy is a replica or fake made to resemble an original.

clue.text: Generously display palms

definitions.meaning: literally showing the insides of the hands, with fingers not closed

explanation.surface: Being bountiful by showing one's palms.
explanation.definitionFit: A giving person is free with money, the opposite of tight-fisted, while the literal sense shows hands spread wide.
